Field Notes / Rental guide

Planning Printed Windscreen for Your Fence

What to consider when adding privacy, dust screening, and project graphics to a temporary perimeter.

Request a quoteCall Richard(317) 296-4015

Rental guide · Fence Wizards

What windscreen adds

Windscreen is fabric fitted across a chain link fence run. Plain screen reduces the view into a construction or service area. Printed screen can also carry a company name, sponsor, development rendering, or leasing message.

Both versions are sold, not rented. The screen stays yours when the temporary fence is collected.

Privacy and dust at the perimeter

Screen can reduce visibility into a site where tools, material, or restoration work would otherwise be on view. On a busy street, it also changes what the public sees along the boundary.

It can help limit dust leaving the perimeter, but it does not replace other dust-control measures used on the job. Explain the purpose of the screen when talking with Richard.

Plan the supporting fence

Screen adds wind load. The fence system, weighting, exposure, and ground conditions need to be considered together. Let Richard know early if the run will be screened.

Screen fits both panels and post-driven chain link. It can also be added later, but the existing support needs to be assessed rather than treating it as a purely visual addition.

Make the graphics useful

Decide who will see the fence and from where. A company name and clear contact information may suit a construction frontage; an event perimeter may need sponsor artwork.

Provide the fence height, printed area, artwork, and required date. The design needs to work across the actual run, including gates and other breaks. Discuss production details before setting an installation deadline.

Ordering and keeping the screen

Ask for plain and printed options if you are weighing the value of graphics. Include windscreen in the scope when comparing fence quotes.

If you want screen fitted to fencing already installed by someone else, describe the existing run to Richard. The fit and support determine whether the work is suitable.
